confusions: The home page has no welfare question, so I had to go to Spending, then to Questions, and scroll a long way down before I found 'How has welfare spending changed?'.
The Spending page shows £33 for social protection but gives no welfare numbers, so I did not know if it was the same thing.
I did not understand what 'Without pensions' means until I read the definition lower down the welfare page.
The welfare page gives spending in four ways (after inflation, per person, share of GDP, share of all spending) and the buttons were hard to tell apart.
The house prices page is very long, with many charts, so I used most of my actions scrolling to find the first-time buyer age and mortgage rate answers.
A line about home ownership for people aged 75 and over was cut off between screens, so I had to find the rest further down the page.
The 10% deposit and the 'years of pay' figures were hard to follow, and I was not sure which year each number was for.
The class sizes page says it has no figures from before 2006, which made me unsure what to compare.
The tuition question asks about fees and loans, but the page only gave the fee figures, not the loans.
The state pension page gives 68 for people born from 6 April 1978, but I did not see the exact wording for people born in 1990, so I chose B with some doubt.
